analysis:
The change touches only docs/architecture/inference.md. I reviewed the two supplied head_text excerpts (lines 1238-2013) and the patch excerpt, which is truncated. No executable code, configuration, keys or deployment settings change, so no new attack surface and no regression against the threat model.

The prose in the reviewed range describes existing controls consistent with the threat model:
- GLM5Next managed load verifies the manifest hash chain and reports the verified aggregate as the published weight hash (relates to T-012/T-027).
- Coordinator-connected mode serves only catalog glm-5.3-flash, behind a hardware requirement and an identity chain.
- The shipped chat template is mandatory, and the tokenizer preflight runs before weight allocation.
- Retained GLM faults quarantine GLM work and charge their bytes to the fleet KV budget.
- The ChunkBatcher drops a frame when no session sink is bound. The doc notes that SendHandle persists across reconnects and does not enforce request-to-session identity; this is described, not introduced, by the PR (TB-002).
- Prompt-token cache reuse never crosses a cache scope. This is consistent with the T-041 cacheSalt scoping.
- The SSD checkpoint staging text is consistent with T-041, with no change to TTL, naming or crypto.
- Media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture, so no KV is reused across images or videos.

The patch excerpt adds only cluster serving-scope/tensorAssistant record-split documentation and a tp-check --layer-stride flag. Both are benchmarking/planning docs, not trust-boundary changes.

Uncertainty: the patch excerpt is truncated and other hunks (head ranges 4866-4891, 6725+, 7318+) are outside the supplied units. I did not verify that the documentation matches the code, and it does not alter the threat model's TB-011/T-053 boundaries.
